subject: Badge scan race condition — Converge on-site duplication / remediation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@summitworks.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Badge scan race condition at Converge — duplicates

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Quick heads-up from on-site ops at Converge today — we've observed badge scans producing duplicate lead entries when multiple kiosks go online at roughly the same time after network flaps. Example: two scans within ~800ms for the same badge ID result in two HubSpot contacts with slightly different source metadata (kiosk-A / kiosk-D).

We're attaching a short device log snippet and the export schema so you can see the payload fields. Can Redwood help triage a short-term debounce/dedupe patch for kiosk uploads? This is causing extra manual cleanup for the expo team and worries the sponsor.

Attaching: device-log-snippet.txt (text)

We'd like a mutual action plan:
- Quick mitigation (hours): client-side debounce or sequence checks?
- Hotfix (1–2 days): server-side dedupe by badge_id + timestamp window with source merge rules
- Postmortem and infra/SDK follow-ups

Available for a call now if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Account Lead, SummitWorks
samir@summitworks.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@summitworks.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Badge scan race condition at Converge — duplicates

Ben / Jonas / Marissa — looping you in. Samir just sent logs from Converge; they’re seeing duplicates when kiosks resync after network blips. Impacts: increased manual merge in HubSpot and sponsor dissatisfaction.

Ask: can we triage a short-lived server-side rule that dedupes by badge_id within a 2s sliding window and prefers the earliest arrival (or merges metadata if the later record has higher-confidence fields)? Goal is a stopgap we can flip on for the next 24–48 hours while we design a more robust SDK debounce.

Ben — confirm if this would break current offline-sync handshake.
Jonas — any quick patch ideas? If we need a feature flag, let’s scope it and ship a small patch.

Samir — we’ll respond with a proposed MAP within the hour. Thanks for flagging.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Field Marketing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Badge scan race condition at Converge — duplicates

On Mon, Mar 16, 2026 at 09:34 AM PDT Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben / Jonas / Marissa — looping you in. Samir just sent logs from Converge; they’re seeing duplicates when kiosks resync after network blips.

Thanks — quick read of the log indicates two near-simultaneous POSTs with identical badge_id and different kiosk_id. Root cause: concurrent local batching + no server-side de-dup window. Short-term plan:

1) Server-side debounce rule (fast): On ingest, if a record arrives with badge_id X and there exists an ingested record for X within the last 2s, drop the duplicate OR merge fields (prefer non-null email / phone). Implement as configuration-backed middleware so we can flip it.
2) SDK patch (next sprint): Add client-side local debounce and monotonic sequence token so resubmits include a sequence number — server will accept highest sequence.
3) HubSpot mapping: ensure merge key uses badge_id + email (if present) so HubSpot dedupe behaves.

I'll draft a minimal patch (approx 100 LOC) and a feature-flag gate. If Ben confirms field devices won't generate out-of-order sequence issues, we can release within a few hours with a rollback flag.

Proposed commit: proposed-debounce-patch.patch (attached)

Jonas Weber
Product Engineer, Runtime
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@summitworks.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Badge scan race condition at Converge — duplicates

Thanks — field ops note: kiosks buffer ~30s of scans when offline and then replay on reconnect. That replay is where we see the bursts. A 2s server window will catch many, but if several devices replay the same badge from different caches at slightly different times we could still see duplicates.

Immediate mitigation suggestion (ops + infra):
- Add server-side 5s window and perform a soft-merge by badge_id. If the second record has higher-confidence fields (email validated by regex or has a non-empty phone), merge into the existing contact rather than create.
- Update HubSpot ingestion mapping so that incoming contact import sets badge_id as external_id and triggers a de-duplication merge (HubSpot import key). I attached the current export schema so we can map fields.

Also, Jamie (on the ground) can push a temporary client-side debounce update to kiosks if we provide the new SDK flag.

Ben Carter
Sr. Program Manager, Field Capture
Redwood Inference
Attachment: badge-export-schema_v2.csv
From: Samir Patel <samir@summitworks.com>

Subject: Re: Badge scan race condition at Converge — duplicates

Appreciate the fast turnaround. We validated the 5s soft-merge approach in a quick local test and it removed >90% of duplicates without losing legitimate separate-scans. Claire from Converge gave thumbs-up to proceed.

Next steps we agreed on call:
- Redwood: flip feature-flag to enable 5s server-side soft-merge (tomorrow morning)
- SummitWorks: deploy temporary client-side debounce to kiosks (next 24 hours)
- Joint QA: run a focused replay test on staging, then verify HubSpot ingestion mapping (use HubSpot company link below)

I've attached the device log snippet we pulled earlier. Schedule: we booked a 30-min staging test for Thu 03/19 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks all — will follow up after the staging run.

Samir
